classDescriptions.stable: Stable mangrove. NDVI follows the seasons, but its long-term level stays high and does not change much.
classDescriptions.gain: Gain. NDVI rose by 0.3 or more between the first and the last 3 years of the record, for example through mangrove growth or regrowth.
classDescriptions.loss: Loss. NDVI fell by 0.3 or more between the first and the last 3 years of the record.
classDescriptions.loss + recovery: Loss and recovery. Mangrove (NDVI 0.3 or more) at the start and the end, but NDVI was below 0.3 for at least two years in between.
classDescriptions.high turnover: High turnover. NDVI moves up and down strongly, with at least a whole year below 0.25 or a lot of back-and-forth change, without one clear direction.
classDescriptions.non-mangrove: Non-mangrove. NDVI stays low: below 0.3 at the start and the end and below 0.25 on average, for example water, bare soil or salt flats.

groups.title: The plots
items: Residual: the deseasonalised NDVI with its slow trend removed. What is left are the month-to-month fluctuations.
AR1 and standard deviation are calculated in a moving window of {window}. Each value describes the window that ends at that month.
The dashed line marks the start of the loss. Only the period before it is analysed, because the drop itself would make the statistics jump.

groups.title: The metrics
items: AR1 (autocorrelation): how much each month's value resembles the month before. A rising AR1 means the ecosystem recovers more slowly from disturbances, a classic sign of an approaching tipping point.
Standard deviation: how large the fluctuations are. A rising standard deviation means the system is becoming less stable.

Skewness and kurtosis: the shape of the fluctuations (asymmetry, and how often extreme values occur). They can also signal an approaching tipping point, but their expected direction depends on the state the system moves towards, so they are shown for context and not used in the verdict.

groups.title: The numbers
items: Kendall's tau: whether a metric keeps going up (towards +1) or down (towards −1) over time; around 0 means no clear trend.
p: how likely a rising trend this strong is by chance. We compare it with simulated series that have the same fluctuations but no trend (AR(1) surrogates). Below 0.05 counts as significant.

groups.title: The verdict
groups.text: An early warning signal needs a significant rise in both AR1 and standard deviation. No warning does not mean nothing happened: it suggests the loss came suddenly, for example after a storm, rather than after a gradual loss of resilience.

pointDescription.breakpointRule: A breakpoint is an abrupt change of at least {threshold} NDVI within 12 months, after which the new level persists for at least 2 years.
pointDescription.ews: Before the drop, we calculated the standard deviation, AR1, kurtosis and skewness of NDVI to look for early warning signals: {verdict}.
pointDescription.verdictEws: an early warning signal was found (AR1 and standard deviation both rose significantly)
pointDescription.verdictNoEws: no early warning signal was found
